work.title: 序聽迷詩所經 (Xuting Mishisuo jing, the Sutra of Jesus the Messiah)

paragraphs.text: The Sutra of Jesus the Messiah, in one scroll

At that time the Messiah explained the law of the Lord of Heaven, Xusuo [?], saying: "There are many differing views, more or fewer; who can explain them? The meaning of the scriptures is hard to [?]; who can explain these matters? Where does the Lord of Heaven appear afterwards? Where is the place in which he abides? Of all the buddhas and non-human beings, the devas [?] and the arhats, who has seen the Lord of Heaven among living beings? No one can see the Lord of Heaven. Who has the power to see the Lord of Heaven? For the face of the Lord of Heaven is like the wind, and who can see the wind?

"Not for a moment [?] does the Lord of Heaven cease to travel through the world, dwelling everywhere. So every person carries the breath of the Lord of Heaven, and only by it are they able to live, and only by it can they dwell at peace in their homes. Wherever the heart's intention reaches, from sunrise to sunset, wherever thought goes, he is there. He dwells in brightness and joy, in stillness and peace; in heaven are all the buddhas. So it is with the wind that moves through the world: there is no place the wind does not reach. The Lord of Heaven always abides in a place of stillness and joy, and there is no place his recompense does not reach. Who among the people of the world knows how the wind moves? They only hear its sound [?] and never once see its form. No one knows its true appearance, whether it is yellow or white or blue, nor does anyone know where the wind dwells in its strength. The Lord of Heaven has his own divine power and abides in one place, and where he abides no one can lay hold of him. He has neither death nor birth, nor any place where he meets with [?]. Since he made heaven and earth [?], he has never been in the world without divine power. He always enjoys everlasting blessed bliss [?].

"When people are in distress, they keep calling on the name of God. Many ignorant people call on spirits, comparing them to the Lord of Heaven, and also make [?] them into honored ones and objects of delight [?], each in the speech of their local customs. I make the distinction that the Lord of Heaven is ever present, always to be trusted, always abiding [?]. The Lord of Heaven knows people's minds well. Who repays God's compassionate grace? We ought to reflect on this and know clearly: do not practice sin and wickedness. Heaven, by its divine power, nourishes [?] the human body until it grows to maturity; living beings too ought to reflect on this. Wherever a person's body, life, organs and breath are, it is the Lord of Heaven who makes them so. All living beings undergo transmigration; the body dwells in hell [?]; therefore it is transformed into fine dust [?]. Let all living beings bring forth good hearts and reflect for themselves: all who are born must die. All living beings [?]. As for the life of living beings, without the wind there is no life. At the hour of death the wind leaves them, and the heart and mind have no wind. They live by the wind, and when the wind leaves living beings there is a time of going and of staying. Why do people not see the wind depart, nor the wind's color, whether crimson or green or some other color? So the wind is not seen. Why then do living beings say, 'Where is the Lord of Heaven?' Living beings further [?] say, 'Why do we not see the Lord of Heaven?' How can living beings who dwell in sin see the Lord of Heaven by themselves? The Lord of Heaven is not like a human body; who then can see [?]? No one dares approach the Lord of Heaven. Only living beings with good fortune and good karmic conditions are at last able to see the Lord of Heaven. In the world no one has ever seen the Lord of Heaven; how then can he be known? Living beings cannot see Heaven by themselves. If they cultivate merit themselves, they will not fall into the evil paths and hell but will attain Heaven. Those with evil karma fall into the evil paths, do not see the bright fruit, and do not attain the heavenly way.

"Let all living beings reflect well. Above heaven and earth are the great [?]; those who serve and support them and labor diligently for the state are granted many official posts and given goods of every kind [?] beyond all measure. If any do not serve the great [?] and do not obey their commands, they receive no office and no reward, but are sentenced to penal servitude or exile, or condemned to death. This does not happen by the will of the great [?]; it is the seed of karma sown in a former life coming to fruit and completion. Those who offend must first consider their own recompense. The Lord of Heaven endured such hardship to establish living beings and the order of living beings [?]. God did not set them far off; a human being is master of himself. Good brings good fortune; evil brings evil consequences.

"Ignorant beings carve [?] wood into camels, elephants, oxen, donkeys, horses and other creatures, and into roe deer and deer; but though they make their forms, they cannot give them life. Living beings have understanding and can weigh their own karma; all that they see they also know for themselves, and all of it is real. So in this present age many beings make for themselves many [?]. All these things are the Lord of Heaven's [?]; yet they cannot give them life. Living beings are deceived, and so they make images of gold, silver images of gods, bronze images, [?] images of gods and wooden images of gods, and they also make all kinds of livestock: a man made like a man, a horse like a horse, an ox like an ox, a donkey like a donkey. Only, they cannot move, nor speak, nor eat; they have no breath, no flesh, no skin, no organs, no bones.

"I do not explain the causes of everything in full. Of all these causes I speak briefly, saying little so that much may be seen, telling people so that they may know good from evil, just as from a great deal of food one tastes a little and so knows which has flavor and which has none. Only for those who serve the Lord of Heaven do I explain the meaning of the scriptures and compose this sutra. In all these matters there is much to lament and many particulars, but the causes are few [?]. Only those who serve the Lord of Heaven and speak of the meaning of Heaven [?]. If someone fears the law of the Lord of Heaven, practices a good heart himself, does good himself, and urges others to do good, that person has received the teaching of the Lord of Heaven and his precepts. If someone constantly does evil and teaches others evil, that person has not received the teaching of the Lord of Heaven; he will suddenly fall into the evil paths, and his life will belong to King Yama. Whoever has received the teaching of the Lord of Heaven always says, 'I have received the precepts, and I teach people to receive the precepts.' People ought to fear the Lord of Heaven and correct their faults every day. All living beings should each fear the Lord of Heaven, who holds and governs all things, who manages and governs the life and death of all living beings and of all the spirits. If living beings fear the Lord of Heaven, they ought also to fear His Holy Majesty. His Holy Majesty was appointed by the Lord of Heaven through the merit of a former life [?]; it is not of himself. The Lord of Heaven [?] himself made His Holy Majesty. All living beings must obey the commands of His Holy Majesty. If anyone does not obey the orders of His Holy Majesty and will not submit, that person is a rebel among living beings [?]. If anyone obeys the commands of His Holy Majesty, he becomes one who understands affairs among men, submits to orders, is a good person, urges others to do good, and does no evil himself; such a person has become one who has received the precepts. If someone receives the precepts and does not fear the Lord of Heaven, that person, even though he follows God's law, has not truly received the precepts; he is a rebel. Third, one must fear one's parents and reverently serve them, comparing them to the Lord of Heaven and the Holy Emperor. If a person first serves the Lord of Heaven and His Holy Majesty, and serves his parents without fail, that person will receive blessing from the Lord of Heaven. There are no more than these three things: first, to serve the Lord of Heaven;

second, to serve His Holy Majesty; third, to serve one's parents. So everything under heaven and on earth is the work of parents [?]. Accordingly, His Holy Majesty is born of the divine. Though in this world one's parents may still be living, living beings with wisdom ought to fear the Lord of Heaven and His Holy Majesty, and to fear their parents, to accept faithfully the law and teaching of the Lord of Heaven, and not to break the precepts. What the Lord of Heaven received and the teaching of the Honored One that was received [?]: first, he caused living beings to worship all the heavens and buddhas. God endured hardship and established heaven and earth only through the causes of purity and power. His Holy Majesty need only diligently [?] the palace of His Holy Majesty. From all the buddhas it was obtained that the person of His Holy Majesty is wholly free [?]. The Lord of Heaven said: "All living beings who turn to evil and the like rebel against the Honored One, and this is not filial." The second vow: be filial to your parents and reverently provide for them. All living beings who are filial to their parents, support them, and honor them without fail will attain the heavenly way at the end of their lives. For house and home exist for serving parents. If living beings had no parents, from whom would they be born? The fourth vow: let whoever has received the precepts bring forth a good heart toward all living beings and harbor no hatred. The fifth vow: let living beings not kill living things themselves, nor urge others to kill, because the life of creatures is no different from the life of humans. The sixth vow: do not commit adultery with another's wife, nor yourself [?]. The seventh vow: do not steal. The eighth: let living beings who see another's wealth and rank, his fields and houses, his male and female slaves, [not] be envious [?]. The ninth vow: [concerning one who] has a good wife and a fine golden house [?], do not bear false witness to slander others. The tenth vow: when you receive something entrusted to you by another, [do not] spend it.

The commands of the Lord of Heaven are very many. When you see someone weak, do not cheat him. When you see a poor person, do not turn your face away; and if a household is starving [?], give generously to drink and eat, giving freely [?]. When you see a man laboring hard, give him something to drink. When you see someone without clothes, give him clothes. Do not keep a hired worker's wages even for a day, for hired workers [?] do not shun cold and frost. When you see laborers [?], do not curse them; the spirits have power, and if you curse them you will surely bring disaster on yourself. If a poor person needs money, give it if you have it; if you have no money to give, send him away with good reason, giving alms out of nothing [?]. When you see someone with a long-standing illness, do not mock him; this is not of his own will. Do not jeer at such people as the sick, the poor, the unclothed and the ragged. Do not cheat others to take their goods; do not wrong others. When someone brings a lawsuit, judge it according to the facts and do not decide it unjustly. When orphans, people who are alone, whether men or women, or widows bring a complaint, do not wrong them, and do not leave them with a grievance. Do not be proud, and do not boast. Do not carry tales or be double-tongued, setting two people to quarrel and fight. All your life [?], do not go to the prefectural and county courts and lay accusations before ignorant officials [?]; [?] one who has received the precepts [?]. Do not direct evil toward others. Always bring forth a good heart toward all living beings; do not wish evil on others [?]. So from much one gauges little [?]. Always do good to all living beings. If anyone sees this and wishes to know [?], one who has received the precepts wrote it [?]. Whoever can follow this sutra is one who has received the precepts. Any living being who cannot follow it has not become one who has received the precepts. All these are the commands of the Lord of Heaven to all the elders and to the great and small, that they should urge one another to do good. This is the first command of the Lord of Heaven [?]; let living beings follow what the Lord of Heaven requires.

Do not let living beings be killed for sacrifice, and do not have any life taken. Yet living beings did not follow this teaching. They killed living things themselves for sacrifice, eating meat and relishing delicacies, using them to deceive [?] false gods, slaughtering sheep and the like. Living beings did not follow this teaching nor the good commands [?]; they turned their backs and did evil, and so turned away from the Lord of Heaven. When the Lord of Heaven saw living beings like this, he had pity on them. He urged them again and again to do good, but they did not obey. So the Lord of Heaven sent a cool wind to a virgin named Mary. The cool wind entered Mary's womb, and in accordance with the Lord of Heaven's teaching Mary at once conceived. Because the Lord of Heaven sent the cool wind to the virgin, she conceived without a husband, so that all living beings would see her conceive without a husband, and the people of the world, seeing it, would say, "The Lord of Heaven has power," and so living beings would be led to faith, purity of heart, and a turning toward good conditions. After conceiving, Mary bore a son named Jesus; his father was the cool wind. Some ignorant beings said, "How can anyone conceive and give birth by the wind?" [?] Yet wherever in the world His Holy Majesty sends a single sheet of edict, all living beings willingly submit. So it is that the Lord of Heaven is in heaven above and governs all heaven and earth.

When Jesus was born, the Messiah being in the world, a bright sign was seen in heaven and on earth: a new star was seen in heaven, as large as a cartwheel, bright and pure, at the place of the Lord of Heaven [?]. [?] He was born in the city of Jerusalem in the land of Fulin. When the Messiah was born, [?] after one year he spoke, preached the law, and did good to living beings. When he was past twelve years old, [he went] to a pure place named Shunan [?], to the one called John, at Tanggu [?]. At first the Messiah's younger brother [?], Fusheng [?], lived in a gorge. From his birth he had never drunk wine or eaten meat, but ate only raw vegetables and honey on the ground. At that time not a few living beings went to John to worship and receive the precepts. Then John had the Messiah enter the Jordan to be washed. After the Messiah had bathed and came out of the water, a cool wind came from heaven, looking like a dove, and settled on the Messiah. From the empty sky a voice said: "The Messiah is my son. All living beings in the world must obey the commands of the Messiah, and all that he commands is good." The Messiah then showed living beings the way of heaven, for this was the command of the Lord of Heaven. He commanded the living beings of the world to stop serving false spirits. Many who heard these words stopped serving false gods, stopped doing evil, and so put their faith in good works. From the age of twelve until he was thirty-two, the Messiah turned all living beings of evil karma toward good works and the good way.

The Messiah had twelve disciples. He then endured suffering [?]. The dead were brought to life, the blind received sight, those whose skin was of a strange color were healed [?], the sick were cured, those possessed by demons had the demons driven out, and the lame were healed. All the sick who came to the Messiah and took hold of his robe were healed. All the evildoers who would not turn to the good way, who did not believe the teaching of the Lord of Heaven, and the impure and greedy people would not let go in this world [?]; they were given to wine and meat and served false gods. The scholars remained [?] and so slandered him [?], and the Jews then wanted to kill him. But because a great many living beings believed this teaching, they could not kill him. Afterward those of evil karma joined with and stirred up [?] the Jews; the people of pure faith [?] took counsel among themselves. They wanted to kill the Messiah but found no way to do it. So they went to the Great King and spoke evil, the people of evil karma reporting evil things [?]. The Messiah did good and taught living beings with still greater zeal.

When he was past thirty-two, those evil people went to the Great King Pilate and accused him, telling Pilate that the Messiah deserved death. The Great King then summoned the evil people to testify together. The Messiah [was brought] before the Great King Pilate, [and they argued that] the Messiah deserved death. The Great King was about to give judgment: "That this man deserves death I have truly neither heard nor seen. This man does not deserve death. Let this matter be decided by the evil people themselves." The Great King said, "I cannot kill him for these evil people," and said, "This man does not deserve death [?]." The Great King Pilate called for water and washed his hands in front of the evil people: "I truly cannot kill this man." The evil people pressed their request all the more: "He must be killed; there is no other way." The Messiah gave himself up to the evil ones for the sake of all living beings, so that the people of the world might know that human life is like a guttering candle. For the living beings of this age he gave himself as an offering and suffered death in their place. The Messiah gave up his own body and so suffered death.

The evil people took the Messiah to another place, a place [?] of wooden beams, called Golgotha [?], and bound him on the wood. They also brought two robbers and placed them on the right [?]. That day they bound the Messiah on the wood at the fifth hour [?]; it was the sixth day, a fast day. He was bound at dawn, and when evening came, darkness covered the four quarters, the earth quaked and the mountains crumbled, all the tombs in the world opened, and all the dead came back to life. Those who saw this still did not believe the teaching of the scriptures [?], that death and life are both through the Messiah. Those among them who had great faith said:
